land.text: Tres Zapotes and the Tuxtlas, 'occupied well past 400 BC, but without the hallmarks of the Olmec culture'

successors.note: The Epi-Olmec page starts that culture c. 300 BCE; the century between is nobody's land.

capitals.name: San Lorenzo (San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán)
capitals.note: Principal centre, not a capital in the political sense: 'the largest city in Mesoamerica from roughly 1200 BCE until 900 BCE'. Coordinates approximate: the page gives none and places the site 'in the southeast portion of the Mexican state of Veracruz' above 'the floodplain of the Coatzacoalcos River'; 'San Lorenzo' is missing from the gazetteer.

capitals.name: La Venta
capitals.note: Principal centre: 'La Venta became the most prominent Olmec center, lasting from 900 BC until its abandonment around 400 BC'. Coordinates from the gazetteer's place entry.

correction.text: the Olmec heartland in 'the modern-day Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco', from the Tuxtlas to La Venta, with San Lorenzo 'the major center of Olmec culture from 1400 BCE to 900 BCE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Olmecs at -650, 550 years after the page's 'roughly 1200 to 400 BC' (infobox 'c. 1200 – 400 BC'). The first Cliopatria shape is reused for the earlier centuries because the heartland did not move; San Lorenzo's page puts it on the Coatzacoalcos floodplain of southeast Veracruz, inside that shape. (Review am-01, 2026-10-18: at grid resolution San Lorenzo (17.75 N, 94.76 W) falls about 13 km outside the -650 shape, so a 20 km circle around the site is added to the shape for -1200..-651)

correction.text: unchanged shape; years -650..-401: La Venta 'lasting from 900 BC until its abandonment around 400 BC'

keyframe_review.note: Years only. 17,603 km2 for the heartland; no infobox area to compare. 'By about 400 BC the major centres of the Olmec civilization had been abandoned', so the shape ends in -401, not -367.

correction.text: the Tuxtlas around Tres Zapotes, which 'continued to be occupied well past 400 BC, but without the hallmarks of the Olmec culture': Epi-Olmec, not Olmec

keyframe_review.note: 5,865 km2 for -366..-351 is the post-Olmec Tuxtlas: the Epi-Olmec culture of Tres Zapotes, which its own page dates c. 300 BCE–250 CE. Not Olmec territory; the epi-olmec-culture dossier uses this shape.

region.text: the Olmec heartland in Veracruz and Tabasco, with San Lorenzo on the Coatzacoalcos floodplain

ledger.note: 1200 BC: the Olmec civilization flourishes from San Lorenzo. 'flourishing in the modern-day Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco from roughly 1200 to 400 BC'; 'The beginnings of Olmec civilization have traditionally been placed between 1400 BC and 1200 BC', newer work moving it 'back to at least 1600–1500 BC'. San Lorenzo 'was the largest city in Mesoamerica from roughly 1200 BCE until 900 BCE' (San Lorenzo page). The year is the page's round figure.

900 BC: the centre shifts from San Lorenzo to La Venta. San Lorenzo 'was all but abandoned around 900 BC at about the same time that La Venta rose to prominence'; 'Widespread destruction of many San Lorenzo monuments also occurred around the 950s BC'. La Venta 'became the most prominent Olmec center, lasting from 900 BC until its abandonment around 400 BC'.

region.text: the heartland: 'By about 400 BC the major centres of the Olmec civilization had been abandoned'

ledger.note: 400 BC: the Olmec centres are abandoned. 'By about 400 BC the major centres of the Olmec civilization had been abandoned'; 'Between 400 and 350 BC, the population in the eastern half of the Olmec heartland dropped precipitously'. Tres Zapotes 'continued to be occupied well past 400 BC, but without the hallmarks of the Olmec culture' (the Epi-Olmec culture, c. 300 BCE–250 CE on its page). Cliopatria runs the row to -351.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture area of centres, not a bordered state; every edge is soft.

sources.title: Olmecs
sources.note: Identity, 1200–400 BC, San Lorenzo to La Venta c. 900 BC, abandonment c. 400 BC, Tres Zapotes after 400 BC.

sources.title: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán
sources.note: San Lorenzo 1400/1200–900 BCE, decline, location on the Coatzacoalcos; no coordinates on the page.

sources.title: Epi-Olmec culture
sources.note: The successor culture, c. 300 BCE–250 CE; used for the successors entry and the -366 verdict.

notes: Type 'culture' is used although the schema describes culture as pre-3400 BCE: the orchestrator's note for this group says to draw Mesoamerican cultures 'as cultures where no state can be shown', and the Olmec page describes a civilization of centres, not a state. Cliopatria's row (-650..-351) misses the first 550 years of the culture and runs 50 years past its end; the keyframes correct both. The second Cliopatria shape (-366..-351) is Epi-Olmec and is handed to the new epi-olmec-culture dossier. San Lorenzo's coordinates are approximate (the page gives none); 'San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán' should be added to the gazetteer. Pages opened: 3 against a budget of 1–2 (the Epi-Olmec page served the successor).
